thesis: Macro conditions do not alter ALAB's fundamental score, but they justify slower purchase pacing. The Fed's September rate increase pressures long-duration valuations, while credit markets remain liquid. The larger company-specific macro risk is geopolitical and structural trade exposure: Taiwan-centered semiconductor production, China-billed revenue and U.S.-China AI/export-control friction. A 0.7 risk-budget multiplier is appropriate pending evidence of lower policy and supply-chain risk.

evidence.claim: The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% on September 16, 2026.
ICE BofA US High Yield OAS was 2.70% on September 17, 2026, indicating relatively benign credit-market stress.
U.S.-China discussions immediately before the cutoff centered on AI, trade, rare earths and Taiwan-sensitive issues, while technology restrictions remained contested.
U.S.-China AI and semiconductor access remained an active strategic dispute before the cutoff, with advanced-chip restrictions and potential further trade measures still under discussion.

counterevidence: ALAB is net cash and internally cash-generative, so tighter credit conditions do not threaten financing.
AI infrastructure capital investment remained robust at the macro level.
Product diversification across standards and platform partners partially reduces any single export-control transmission channel.
unknowns: Exact end-demand share attributable to China versus billing through manufacturing partners.
Sensitivity of hyperscale AI capex to further rate increases.
falsifiers: A durable easing cycle with stable inflation would reduce discount-rate pressure.
Meaningful supply-chain diversification away from Taiwan would reduce geopolitical transmission.
Broader export controls covering ALAB's products or end customers would raise the overlay risk.
